{"idea":{"slug":"console-audit-log","title":"Every change made in the web console is written to an audit log a teammate can read back.","type":"feature","feature":"F2","milestone":"Harbor 2.0","priority":"P3","excerpt":"A setting changed in the console leaves no trace; when a mirror stops, nobody can say who changed what, or when.","path":"specs/ideas/console-audit-log.md","state":{"kind":"idea","id":"console-audit-log","state":"open","stage":"idea","command":"/spec new console-audit-log","reason":"the story is shaped but has no spec"}},"page":{"frontmatter":{"type":"feature","feature":"F2","milestone":"Harbor 2.0","priority":"P3","status":"idea"},"html":"

/spec

Type

feature

Repo

harbor Slug: console-audit-log

Goal (one sentence)

Every change made in the web console is written to an audit log a teammate can read back.

Problem

A setting changed in the console leaves no trace; when a mirror stops, nobody can say who changed what, or when.

In

  • One audit line per console write: time, actor, setting, old and new value
  • An audit page in the console, newest first

Out

  • No export, no retention policy of its own

Done means (observable)

  • A console write appends exactly one audit line → bun-test
  • The audit page lists the newest line first → e2e

Guard rails

  • No credential value ever reaches an audit line (F0)

{"idea":{"slug":"registry-webhooks","title":"A push to an upstream repository triggers a sync of that repository within a minute, without waiting for the schedule.","type":"feature","feature":"F7","milestone":"Harbor 1.0","priority":"P2","excerpt":"A moved upstream tag reaches the mirror only on the next scheduled run, so a build in between pulls the old digest.","path":"specs/ideas/registry-webhooks.md","state":{"kind":"idea","id":"registry-webhooks","state":"open","stage":"idea","command":"/spec new registry-webhooks","reason":"the story is shaped but has no spec"}},"page":{"frontmatter":{"type":"feature","feature":"F7","milestone":"Harbor 1.0","priority":"P2","status":"idea"},"html":"

/spec

Type

feature

Repo

harbor Slug: registry-webhooks

Goal (one sentence)

A push to an upstream repository triggers a sync of that repository within a minute, without waiting for the schedule.

Problem

A moved upstream tag reaches the mirror only on the next scheduled run, so a build in between pulls the old digest.

In

  • A webhook endpoint on the API that accepts a registry's push event
  • One sync of the named repository per event, deduplicated while one is running

Out

  • No webhook for retention runs
  • No registry outside the test matrix

Done means (observable)

  • One push event starts exactly one sync of that repository → bun-test
  • An event for a repository not in the config starts nothing and is logged → bun-test

Guard rails

  • The endpoint binds to loopback unless --listen names another address (F0)

{"frontmatter":{"title":"Harbor","lang":"en"},"html":"

Harbor — technical documentation

Overview

Harbor mirrors the container manifests a team depends on into the team's own registry. One command, harbor sync, copies every listed manifest byte for byte, and running it again is a no-op. A small web console shows each run, and retention policies keep the mirror bounded.

Stack

PartBuilt withNotes
CLIBun, TypeScriptharbor sync, one binary
APIBun, TypeScriptport 8080, loopback by default
ConsoleAngularport 4200 in development

Architecture

The CLI reads the config, resolves each upstream manifest and pushes it whole to the target, or not at all. Every run is recorded in the history the console reads through the API.

Risks

  • The config loader rewrite touches every package at once; its parity snapshots are the only guard.
  • A push interrupted mid-manifest must leave nothing behind in the target; the atomic-push probe holds it.
